title: CBT Basics (The Cognitive Triangle)
shortDefinition: The psychological framework showing how our Thoughts, Emotions, and Behaviors constantly influence and feed into one another.
dailyExample: Thought: 'I am going to fail this presentation.' -> Emotion: Physical anxiety & racing pulse -> Behavior: Canceling the presentation or procrastinating prep -> Reinforces Thought.
psychologyTheory: Pioneered by Dr. Aaron T. Beck in the 1960s. CBT posits that emotional distress is rarely caused by external events themselves, but by the interpretation and meaning we assign to them.
inTherapy: We map out automatic negative thoughts (ANTs), examine cognitive distortions (catastrophizing, mind-reading, black-and-white thinking), and experiment with more balanced thoughts.
practicalTakeaway: You cannot always control the first automatic thought that enters your head, but you have full agency over whether you buy into it as absolute truth.
